I have been farming this land for 30 years. My mother farmed before me. I know this soil, I know when the rains come and when they do not. I do not need to read a book to know what works here in Quzhou.

My 7 mu is split the way I have always done it — about 5 mu runs in the wheat-maize rotation, and I keep about 2 mu separate for peanut in spring. The same land cannot do everything at once.

**Wheat** goes in around Hanlu, early October. I will buy improved seed from the seed store in town, the kind the neighbors are also using — Jimai variety, reliable. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and urea at jointing. I irrigate before sowing to get the soil moist, then again at jointing, heading, and grain filling — four times. My pump is reliable. I spray herbicide in winter and fungicide in April when the flag leaf comes out. Rotary tillage before seeding to turn in the maize stubble.

**Maize** I plant right after wheat harvest in June — no plowing, just direct seeding to save time and keep moisture. My son helps during those days before going back to his job in the city. I use hybrid seed, same brand I used last year, good germination. Fertilizer heavier here than wheat. Two or three irrigations if August is dry. Spray for corn borer if I see the damage starting.

**Peanut** on the 2 mu separate plot. Spring peanut, planted after Qingming when soil warms up. I plow this plot deeply — peanut needs loose soil for the pods to swell. Less nitrogen needed, peanut finds its own. I water three times: at flowering, pegging, and pod swelling. Harvest in September before the maize.

With some family off-farm I do most of this myself with occasional hired labor at peak times. I keep things simple — what has worked for 30 years will work again.
